HM03-q01-z9oxuc: Class 3 flammable liquids is one of the 5 no-smoking classes.
Class 5 oxidizers is one of the 5 no-smoking classes.
HM03-q02-21rv2v: It is illegal to move a vehicle with leaking HazMat, even to a truck stop.
Don't patch it and haul it; leaking packages must not be transported.
HM03-q03-1qkajn: 1, 4 and 5 is the closed-cargo-space list; cargo heater rules cover 1, 2.1 and 3.
Classes 6 and 8 have no cargo heater rules; the 3 classes are 1, 2.1 and 3.
HM03-q04-qqvm6t: Corrosives are not on the closed-cargo-space list; that list is Class 1, 4 and 5.
Class 9 is not on the closed-cargo-space list; that list is Class 1, 4 and 5.
HM03-q05-nzer5w: Stainless steel contains iron; the liner must be nonmetallic or a nonferrous metal.
Not any metal: the floor must be tight and the liner nonmetallic or nonferrous (no iron).
HM03-q06-63158m: Turn the engine off before loading or unloading any explosives.
Cargo heaters must be disabled (power off, fuel tanks drained) before loading explosives.
HM03-q07-7nyoke: Never accept an explosives package with dampness or an oily stain.
A shipper's signature doesn't change it; don't accept an explosives package with an oily stain.
HM03-q08-6t3rxb: An endorsement isn't enough; transfers on a public road are allowed only in an emergency.
An emergency transfer is allowed, with red warning reflectors, flags or electric lanterns set out.
HM03-q09-rl2t70: Never load nitric acid above any other product, so not on a top tier.
The nitric acid rule is about height: it is never loaded above any other product.
HM03-q10-hd1hgt: Other corrosives aren't on the list; the list is Div. 1.4, 4.1, 4.3, Class 5 and Div. 2.3 Zone B.
Empty pallets aren't HazMat; the list is Div. 1.4, 4.1, 4.3, Class 5 and Div. 2.3 Zone B.
HM03-q11-n5ygct: Cylinders must ride upright; lying flat is only for cylinders with the relief valve in the vapor space.
Cylinders are held upright in racks attached to the vehicle or in boxes that keep them from turning over.
HM03-q12-9ziqvd: Fill level doesn't matter; only a cylinder designed with the relief valve in the vapor space may lie down.
Only a cylinder designed with the relief valve in the vapor space may be loaded lying down.
HM03-q13-qaqxn0: A closed van is fine; POISON packages must never go in the cab or sleeper, or with food.
Skin creams are not food, so they may ride with POISON packages.
HM03-q14-q6wj8c: The total transport index in one vehicle must not exceed 50, not 20.
The limit is 50, not 40; 40 is only a row boundary in the separation table.
HM03-q15-ht72kn: Position doesn't help; cyanides must not be loaded with acids or corrosives like battery acid.
Weight doesn't matter; cyanides and acids never share a vehicle.
HM03-q16-0tc7bd: Where the food sits doesn't change the rule; the poison must be overpacked in an approved way.
Stacking doesn't change the rule; the poison package must be overpacked in an approved way.
HM03-q17-hjt1aj: The Do Not Load table pairs charged storage batteries with Division 1.1, not Class 9.
The Do Not Load table pairs charged storage batteries with Division 1.1 explosives.
HM03-q18-295wov: 119 gallons or less is nonbulk; a cargo tank is bulk packaging permanently attached to a vehicle.
That describes a portable tank; a cargo tank stays on the vehicle while loaded and unloaded.
HM03-q19-0stcgg: Staying on the vehicle describes a cargo tank; a portable tank is loaded and unloaded off it.
No inspection site is involved; a portable tank is loaded or unloaded off the vehicle.
HM03-q20-w0gykg: 2 inches is a portable-tank letter height; ID numbers are black, 100 mm (3.9 in) tall.
1 inch is the small-tank letter height; ID numbers are black, 100 mm (3.9 in) tall.
HM03-q21-9tbcik: One side is never enough; at 1,000 gallons or more, show it on each side and each end.
2 opposite sides is for tanks under 1,000 gallons; 1,200 gallons needs each side and each end.
HM03-q22-ao1jze: The watcher must be within 25 feet of the tank, not 100, with a clear view.
The watcher must be within 25 feet of the tank, alert, with a clear view.
HM03-q23-3zptmi: Grounding after closing is too late; ground before opening and keep it until after closing.
Grounding doesn't depend on the engine; ground before opening the filling hole.
HM03-q24-1jpxh5: Wrong order: turn the engine off after the transfer and before unhooking the hose.
Turn the engine off after the transfer; unhook all connections before coupling or moving a cargo tank.
HM03-q25-xfykyu: Close all manholes and valves before moving, no matter how small the amount.
Close all manholes and valves before moving, no matter how short the distance.
